text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Half of the 100,000 tickets to Michael Jackson's concert were sold or booked on the first day of sale.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann opened a new block at Tallinn Prison.
- The defence lawyer of Tiit Madisson, jailed for allegedly organising a coup, has appealed to the human rights commission in Strasbourg.
- Italian foreign ministry chancellor Boris Bianchieri Chiappori told Siimann that Italy is interested in a visa-free travel deal with Estonia.
- Foreign Minister Tooomas Hendrik Ilves will meet EU and NATO leaders during a visit to Brussels.
- Foreign students studying in Estonia demand an agreement with the government fixing the tuition fee. The government allowed a sudden increase of fees last summer.
- The police elite K-squad anti-terrorism unit practiced an air assault on a passenger ship. 18 men were landed aboard the ferry "Regina Baltica" from a helicopter.
- The meat producers confederation submitted an appeal against protective tariffs to the economy minister.
- The Baltic Ship Repair Plant in Tallinn is applying for a major order from Russia for the construction of oil tankers worth $60 million.
- The newspaper complained that the control over the securities market is still weak and nobody is responsible for the data published in a firm's prospectus.
